title: Examining the impact of small-amplitude hydraulic transients on biofilm development and adhesion in a full-scale, controlled water distribution environment
content:
Environ. Sci.: Adv., 2026, Advance Article
DOI: 10.1039/D5VA00415B, Paper
Open Access
  This article is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 3.0 Unported Licence.
Mariele de Souza Parra Agostinho, Artur Sass Braga, Benjamin Anderson, Yves Filion, Cristovão Vicente Scapulatempo Fernandes
Moderate hydraulic transients (∼20 kPa) enhanced biofilm growth/adhesion; stronger ones caused detachment but created resilient films. Small transients shaped biofilm distribution in water pipes, proving flow variability drives microbial stability.
